2:19.ar: أَوۡ كَصَيِّبࣲ مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ فِيهِ ظُلُمَٰتࣱ وَرَعۡدࣱ وَبَرۡقࣱ يَجۡعَلُونَ أَصَٰبِعَهُمۡ فِيٓ ءَاذَانِهِم مِّنَ ٱلصَّوَٰعِقِ حَذَرَ ٱلۡمَوۡتِۚ وَٱللَّهُ مُحِيطُۢ بِٱلۡكَٰفِرِينَ
2:19.en: Or like a rainstorm from the sky, wherein is darkness, thunder and the flash of lightning. They thrust their fingers in their ears by reason of the thunder-claps, for fear of death, Allah encompasseth the disbelievers (in His guidance, His omniscience and His omnipotence)

2:255.ar: ٱللَّهُ لَآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ ٱلۡحَيُّ ٱلۡقَيُّومُۚ لَا تَأۡخُذُهُۥ سِنَةࣱ وَلَا نَوۡمࣱۚ لَّهُۥ مَا فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَمَا فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِۗ مَن ذَا ٱلَّذِي يَشۡفَعُ عِندَهُۥٓ إِلَّا بِإِذۡنِهِۦۚ يَعۡلَمُ مَا بَيۡنَ أَيۡدِيهِمۡ وَمَا خَلۡفَهُمۡۖ وَلَا يُحِيطُونَ بِشَيۡءࣲ مِّنۡ عِلۡمِهِۦٓ إِلَّا بِمَا شَآءَۚ وَسِعَ كُرۡسِيُّهُ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضَۖ وَلَا يَـُٔودُهُۥ حِفۡظُهُمَاۚ وَهُوَ ٱلۡعَلِيُّ ٱلۡعَظِيمُ
2:255.en: Allah! There is no deity save Him, the Alive, the Eternal. Neither slumber nor sleep overtaketh Him. Unto Him belongeth whatsoever is in the heavens and whatsoever is in the earth. Who is he that intercedeth with Him save by His leave? He knoweth that which is in front of them and that which is behind them, while they encompass nothing of His knowledge save what He will. His throne includeth the heavens and the earth, and He is never weary of preserving them. He is the Sublime, the Tremendous

41:54.ar: أَلَآ إِنَّهُمۡ فِي مِرۡيَةࣲ مِّن لِّقَآءِ رَبِّهِمۡۗ أَلَآ إِنَّهُۥ بِكُلِّ شَيۡءࣲ مُّحِيطُۢ
41:54.en: How! Are they still in doubt about the meeting with their Lord? Lo! Is not He surrounding all things

65:12.ar: ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِي خَلَقَ سَبۡعَ سَمَٰوَٰتࣲ وَمِنَ ٱلۡأَرۡضِ مِثۡلَهُنَّۖ يَتَنَزَّلُ ٱلۡأَمۡرُ بَيۡنَهُنَّ لِتَعۡلَمُوٓاْ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيۡءࣲ قَدِيرࣱ وَأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ قَدۡ أَحَاطَ بِكُلِّ شَيۡءٍ عِلۡمَۢا
65:12.en: Allah it is who hath created seven heavens, and of the earth the like thereof. The commandment cometh down among them slowly, that ye may know that Allah is Able to do all things, and that Allah surroundeth all things in knowledge

72:28.ar: لِّيَعۡلَمَ أَن قَدۡ أَبۡلَغُواْ رِسَٰلَٰتِ رَبِّهِمۡ وَأَحَاطَ بِمَا لَدَيۡهِمۡ وَأَحۡصَىٰ كُلَّ شَيۡءٍ عَدَدَۢا
72:28.en: That He may know that they have indeed conveyed the messages of their Lord. He surroundeth all their doings, and He keepeth count of all things

17:60.ar: وَإِذۡ قُلۡنَا لَكَ إِنَّ رَبَّكَ أَحَاطَ بِٱلنَّاسِۚ وَمَا جَعَلۡنَا ٱلرُّءۡيَا ٱلَّتِيٓ أَرَيۡنَٰكَ إِلَّا فِتۡنَةࣰ لِّلنَّاسِ وَٱلشَّجَرَةَ ٱلۡمَلۡعُونَةَ فِي ٱلۡقُرۡءَانِۚ وَنُخَوِّفُهُمۡ فَمَا يَزِيدُهُمۡ إِلَّا طُغۡيَٰنࣰ ا كَبِيرࣰ ا
17:60.en: And (it was a warning) when we told thee: Lo! thy Lord encompasseth mankind, and We appointed the sight which We showed thee as an ordeal for mankind, and (likewise) the Accursed Tree in the Qur'an. We warn them, but it increaseth them in naught save gross impiety

85:20.en: And Allah, all unseen, surroundeth them

35:44.ar: أَوَلَمۡ يَسِيرُواْ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ فَيَنظُرُواْ كَيۡفَ كَانَ عَٰقِبَةُ ٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبۡلِهِمۡ وَكَانُوٓاْ أَشَدَّ مِنۡهُمۡ قُوَّةࣰۚ وَمَا كَانَ ٱللَّهُ لِيُعۡجِزَهُۥ مِن شَيۡءࣲ فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَلَا فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِۚ إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ عَلِيمࣰ ا قَدِيرࣰ ا
35:44.en: Have they not travelled in the land and seen the nature of the consequence for those who were before them, and they were mightier than these in power? Allah is not such that aught in the heavens or in the earth escapeth Him. Lo! He is the Wise, the Mighty

6:59.ar: ۞وَعِندَهُۥ مَفَاتِحُ ٱلۡغَيۡبِ لَا يَعۡلَمُهَآ إِلَّا هُوَۚ وَيَعۡلَمُ مَا فِي ٱلۡبَرِّ وَٱلۡبَحۡرِۚ وَمَا تَسۡقُطُ مِن وَرَقَةٍ إِلَّا يَعۡلَمُهَا وَلَا حَبَّةࣲ فِي ظُلُمَٰتِ ٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَلَا رَطۡبࣲ وَلَا يَابِسٍ إِلَّا فِي كِتَٰبࣲ مُّبِينࣲ‏
6:59.en: And with Him are the keys of the Invisible. None but He knoweth them. And He knoweth what is in the land and the sea. Not a leaf falleth but He knoweth it, not a grain amid the darkness of the earth, naught of wet or dry but (it is noted) in a clear record

4:108.ar: يَسۡتَخۡفُونَ مِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ وَلَا يَسۡتَخۡفُونَ مِنَ ٱللَّهِ وَهُوَ مَعَهُمۡ إِذۡ يُبَيِّتُونَ مَا لَا يَرۡضَىٰ مِنَ ٱلۡقَوۡلِۚ وَكَانَ ٱللَّهُ بِمَا يَعۡمَلُونَ مُحِيطًا
4:108.en: They seek to hide from men and seek not to hide from Allah. He is with them when by night they hold discourse displeasing unto Him. Allah ever surroundeth what they do

4:105.ar: إِنَّآ أَنزَلۡنَآ إِلَيۡكَ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ بِٱلۡحَقِّ لِتَحۡكُمَ بَيۡنَ ٱلنَّاسِ بِمَآ أَرَىٰكَ ٱللَّهُۚ وَلَا تَكُن لِّلۡخَآئِنِينَ خَصِيمࣰ ا
4:105.en: Lo! We reveal unto thee the Scripture with the truth, that thou mayst judge between mankind by that which Allah showeth thee. And be not thou a pleader for the treacherous

4:106.ar: وَٱسۡتَغۡفِرِ ٱللَّهَۖ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ كَانَ غَفُورࣰ ا رَّحِيمࣰ ا
4:106.en: And seek forgiveness of Allah. Lo! Allah is ever Forgiving, Merciful

4:107.ar: وَلَا تُجَٰدِلۡ عَنِ ٱلَّذِينَ يَخۡتَانُونَ أَنفُسَهُمۡۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يُحِبُّ مَن كَانَ خَوَّانًا أَثِيمࣰ ا
4:107.en: And plead not on behalf of (people) who deceive themselves. Lo! Allah loveth not one who is treacherous and sinful

3:120.ar: إِن تَمۡسَسۡكُمۡ حَسَنَةࣱ تَسُؤۡهُمۡ وَإِن تُصِبۡكُمۡ سَيِّئَةࣱ يَفۡرَحُواْ بِهَاۖ وَإِن تَصۡبِرُواْ وَتَتَّقُواْ لَا يَضُرُّكُمۡ كَيۡدُهُمۡ شَيۡـًٔاۗ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ بِمَا يَعۡمَلُونَ مُحِيطࣱ‏
3:120.en: If a lucky chance befall you, it is evil unto them, and if disaster strike you they rejoice thereat. But if ye persevere and keep from evil their guile will never harm you. Lo! Allah is Surrounding what they do

19:94.en: Verily He knoweth them and numbereth them with (right) numbering

19:95.en: And each one of them will come unto Him on the Day of Resurrection, alone

58:6.ar: يَوۡمَ يَبۡعَثُهُمُ ٱللَّهُ جَمِيعࣰ ا فَيُنَبِّئُهُم بِمَا عَمِلُوٓاْۚ أَحۡصَىٰهُ ٱللَّهُ وَنَسُوهُۚ وَٱللَّهُ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيۡءࣲ شَهِيدٌ
58:6.en: On the day when Allah will raise them all together and inform them of what they did. Allah hath kept account of it while they forgot it. And Allah is Witness over all things

zHDbZ-lntT0.title: The Glorious Names of Allah: The All-Encompassing, Al-Muhit
zHDbZ-lntT0.one_line: Al-Muhit: an umbrella name meaning Allah surrounds all things by knowledge, dominance and care, appearing wherever sins are layered and schemes complex.
zHDbZ-lntT0.summary: He calls Al-Muhit an umbrella name under which some twenty-five other names fall, which is why it always stands alone in the Quran. It means the One who encompasses everything by His knowledge, His dominance and His care, a figurative surrounding from every angle. He traces where it appears: early in Al-Baqarah about the disbelievers, in Ayat al-Kursi, at the close of Fussilat, At-Talaq and Al-Jinn, in the verse reassuring the Prophet that his Lord encompasses the people, and after the believers burned in the trench in Al-Buruj. The pattern is that the name comes when a sin is complex, involving thought, intention, word and deed together. His main illustration is the theft from Rifa'ah, where a family conspired to frame their Jewish neighbour by burying a stolen shield in his yard, and the verses that came down clearing the innocent man and telling the Prophet not to defend those who betray. He adds the hypocrites who withdrew before Uhud hoping for the Muslims' defeat, and the verses that Allah has counted every person and every deed people themselves forgot. Living with the name means accepting that every thought and feeling is known, that no argument can outmatch Him, and so surrendering with humility, which is the meaning of Islam.

outline.heading: Opening
An umbrella name
outline.gist: One of the early, unique names, without synonyms, under which many other names fall.

outline.heading: Encompassing by knowledge, dominance and care
outline.gist: Al-Muhit encompasses all things through what He knows, what He controls and what He cares for, so other names sit beneath it.

outline.heading: Meaning of the word and why it stands alone
outline.gist: The root means to surround, used figuratively; the name appears seven times and never paired, since it already holds about twenty-five names.

outline.heading: First appearance: disbelievers and complex sin
outline.gist: Early in Al-Baqarah it describes the disbelievers; it comes whenever a sin has several layers of thought, intention, word and deed.

outline.heading: In Ayat al-Kursi
outline.gist: In the weightiest verse, people encompass nothing of His knowledge except what He wills.

outline.heading: End of Fussilat: doubt about meeting Him
outline.gist: They doubt meeting their Lord, yet He encompasses everything, so thoughts and the actions built on them are all accounted for.

outline.heading: End of At-Talaq and Al-Jinn
outline.gist: His command descends through seven heavens and earths and He encompasses all by knowledge; He encompasses what the messengers have and counts everything by number.

outline.heading: Your Lord encompasses the people
outline.gist: A verse meant to reassure the Prophet and the Muslims that no one escapes or is forgotten, while we encompass nothing of His knowledge.

outline.heading: The people of the trench
outline.gist: The name is a hallmark of grave deeds; at the end of Al-Buruj Allah encompasses both those who burned the believers and those burned, and accountability is coming.

outline.heading: Nothing escapes Him; the keys of the unseen
outline.gist: Nothing in the heavens or earth escapes Him, and He knows every falling leaf and every grain, which defines the name.

outline.heading: They hide from people but not from Allah
outline.gist: The verse about those who conceal their plotting from people while Allah is with them introduces his main story.

outline.heading: The stolen shield and the trail of wheat
outline.gist: Two men stole wheat and a father's shield from a new Muslim; his nephew followed a trail of wheat to their house and told the Prophet.

outline.heading: Framing the Jewish neighbour
outline.gist: Seen, the thieves had family swear they were home, buried the shield in a Jewish neighbour's yard and accused him; the shield was found there.

outline.heading: Revelation clears the innocent man
outline.gist: Verses told the Prophet to seek forgiveness for his ruling and not to defend those who betray; betrayal, scheming and harm is where the name appears.

outline.heading: The hypocrites who withdrew before Uhud
outline.gist: Three hundred left hoping the Muslims would be destroyed; they grieve at your good and rejoice at your harm, but patience and taqwa make their plots harmless.

outline.heading: He counted all that we forgot
outline.gist: He has counted every person and each comes alone; deeds we have long forgotten are all recorded, which comforts and frightens.

outline.heading: Living with the name: surrender
outline.gist: He knows every detail, thought and feeling from every angle, so no argument beats Him; all we can do is hope for mercy and submit with humility, the meaning of Islam.

8:41.ar: ۞وَٱعۡلَمُوٓاْ أَنَّمَا غَنِمۡتُم مِّن شَيۡءࣲ فَأَنَّ لِلَّهِ خُمُسَهُۥ وَلِلرَّسُولِ وَلِذِي ٱلۡقُرۡبَىٰ وَٱلۡيَتَٰمَىٰ وَٱلۡمَسَٰكِينِ وَٱبۡنِ ٱلسَّبِيلِ إِن كُنتُمۡ ءَامَنتُم بِٱللَّهِ وَمَآ أَنزَلۡنَا عَلَىٰ عَبۡدِنَا يَوۡمَ ٱلۡفُرۡقَانِ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡتَقَى ٱلۡجَمۡعَانِۗ وَٱللَّهُ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيۡءࣲ قَدِيرٌ
8:41.en: And know that whatever ye take as spoils of war, lo! a fifth thereof is for Allah, and for the messenger and for the kinsman (who hath need) and orphans and the needy and the wayfarer, if ye believe in Allah and that which We revealed unto Our slave on the Day of Discrimination, the day when the two armies met. TRZ5FPYu-DE.title: The Laws of Success/Victory 4: Waqf (Endowment)
TRZ5FPYu-DE.one_line: The third money law of Al-Anfal: waqf, the Prophet's model of centralized endowment, and his call for a city-wide Muslim endowment fund.
TRZ5FPYu-DE.summary: He opens on the all-too-familiar images from Gaza, Sudan, Syria, Iraq, Yemen and Kosovo, which he reads as wake-up calls; the ummah will rise from under the rubble, and our only job is to push the wheel the right way. Al-Anfal's laws must be followed in full, not ninety-nine percent of them. The third money law is waqf. The verse assigning a fifth of the spoils to Allah and His Messenger introduced, for the first time, wealth owned by no one. He traces the Prophet's teaching: Umar's best land made into an endowment that cannot be sold, gifted or inherited; Uthman's well; the narrations on ongoing charity, a masjid, a mushaf or a refugee house that follow you into the grave. Without waqf and centralized wealth, he argues, Islam would never have left the Hijaz, and he reads Abu Bakr's wars over zakat as a defence of that centralization. He then turns to the community: budgets are pathetic, institutions should be funded on the services they offer rather than fundraising talent, and a trust breach is growing. He asks everyone to make something waqf, even one car, one table or their time, and dreams of a single city-wide endowment fund. Think long term, get over egos and names.

outline.heading: Opening
Three laws about money
outline.gist: He has grouped together the surah's three laws about money: materialism, the pitfall the surah is named after; preparation, including its financial side; and today's third.

outline.heading: Pictures all too familiar
outline.gist: The scenes from Gaza and Sudan repeat three decades of the same images in Iraq, Afghanistan, Syria, Yemen, Libya and Kosovo: the same people, different culprits. Allah sends these as wake-up calls to rouse the ummah from its slumber.

outline.heading: From under the rubble the ummah will stand
outline.gist: He is certain the ummah will rise again from under the rubble, sooner than we think. All we can do in a short life is be a positive force on the right side of the equation, pushing the wheel in the right direction.

outline.heading: Concise laws, and all of them
outline.gist: The ten-page surah gives its laws concisely and directly, as laws should be. Unless we follow all of them, not half, three quarters or 99 percent, we will keep struggling.

outline.heading: The verse of the fifth: where endowment began
outline.gist: The verse assigning a fifth of the spoils to Allah and His Messenger was the first time Islamic law set aside wealth owned by no one. Histories credit Marcus Aurelius's endowments for philosophers, but the first documented endowments were madrasas and universities in North Africa, and the concept began with the Prophet through this verse.

outline.heading: Umar's best land
outline.gist: Umar came with the best land he had ever owned and asked what to do. The Prophet told him to make the land itself a waqf: never sold, gifted or inherited, its produce going to the needy, travellers, refugees and captives, its caretaker eating from it reasonably but not for profit.

outline.heading: Uthman's well and the deeds that continue
outline.gist: Uthman bought a well so Muslims could drink freely, with any sales to others returning to the Muslims. The hadith in Muslim: when a person dies, one of the three things that continue is ongoing charity, a form of endowment.

outline.heading: What follows you into the grave
outline.gist: The fuller narration in Ibn Majah lists the good deeds that follow you: a child raised well, charity, knowledge that lives on, a mushaf, a masjid, a home for travellers. That was the birth of waqf.

outline.heading: Without waqf, Islam would not have left the Hijaz
outline.gist: He stakes his life on it: without waqf the ummah would never have left the Arabian Peninsula. What let Islam spread was the model the Prophet began himself.

outline.heading: Wealth gathered centrally, then a growing treasury
outline.gist: In the Prophet's time wealth was brought centrally and distributed almost at once because need was high. By Umar's time there was a treasury whose wealth generated more wealth to strengthen the ummah.

outline.heading: Abu Bakr's wars over centralized zakat
outline.gist: The so-called apostasy wars were tribes refusing to pay zakat centrally, not leaving Islam. Had Abu Bakr not fought for centralization, Islam would have stopped at the northern borders of Arabia. The Prophet's legacy lies in what he did as well as what he said.

outline.heading: A legacy that funded masajid and universities
outline.gist: The context of a Muslim state differs, but the idea still applies to communities. Throughout history Muslims funded their masajid and universities through waqf.

outline.heading: Family endowments, and every Companion with means
outline.gist: People made their estates a waqf for their children so the land would keep providing, and such family endowments still exist. A Companion reports that none of the Companions with some wealth failed to make part of it waqf, and we must do the same.

outline.heading: Pathetic budgets
outline.gist: He does not mean this centre but the Muslim community at large: the budgets discussed for advocacy, schools and social support are pathetic. NCCM, Hikma and the MRC need far better support.

outline.heading: Fund services, not fundraising talent
outline.gist: Support should be allocated by the services an institution offers, not its skill in marketing or fundraising. Otherwise the same complaints and bickering continue because resources are used badly.

outline.heading: Make something waqf
outline.gist: One car of a taxi company one day a week, one restaurant table, one clinic seat a week; with no money, make your time waqf. I'tikaf in the coming Ramadan means making yourself a waqf for Allah. Endless fundraising, hands in people's pockets, is not sustainable.

outline.heading: Interlude
A city-wide endowment fund
outline.gist: The centre will pilot an endowment fund, but his dream is one fund for the whole city, run by trustworthy experts from every organization, distributing by need and the services offered rather than fundraising talent.

outline.heading: Not how Muslims run communities
outline.gist: Ticketed fundraising dinners that make people feel important are not the Muslim way. Over ten years he has seen money raised without knowing where it went; he believes the people running institutions are clean, but distribution is poor.

outline.heading: A trust breach
outline.gist: People are tired of giving without seeing output, and a trust breach is growing. Without funding our institutions the masajid and advocacy groups will fail, so the model has to change to the one the Prophet pioneered.

outline.heading: Others took the concept we built
outline.gist: Endowment funds exist everywhere except in Muslim communities, and the vocabulary itself came from Muslims. Non-profits that generate their own wealth could be built at city, provincial and national level.

outline.heading: The hospital donor wall
outline.gist: He walks daily past a huge hospital wall of major donors with not one Muslim institution on it, while institutions Muslims dislike gave millions. Unless we are truly few and poor, it cannot be excused.

outline.heading: Big heads and small hearts
outline.gist: It is a lack of will and cooperation: too many egos. Children who could have learned the language of the Quran lose out, and the vulnerable fall into substance abuse and crime instead of being supported.

outline.heading: Think a decade or two ahead
outline.gist: He is not a money person, but the concept of waqf is the Prophet's. Start small and, if it works, bring everyone to the table, for your children a decade or two from now, so the next generation is not still describing civilians buried under their homes.

outline.heading: Get over our names
outline.gist: With hospitals evacuated and journalists shot, a different future needs bigger, longer thinking and letting go of our names and organizations, which mean nothing on the Day of Judgment when we are asked what we could have done.

8JUcD_qp0Ao.title: The Glorious Names of Allah: The Protecting Guardian, Al-Wali
8JUcD_qp0Ao.one_line: Al-Wali as a two-way bond: you take Allah as protector, He must choose you back, and you earn it by guarding someone vulnerable.
8JUcD_qp0Ao.summary: He renders Al-Wali as the Protecting Guardian and contrasts it with Al-Wakil. Taking Allah as your trustee is an open contract that is sealed the moment you rely on Him, but Al-Wali is two-way: you declare Him your guardian and then hope He takes you as His. He grounds the word in everyday Arabic usage, the guardian a pupil must bring to school, the orphan who has none, and the wali of a bride, which he defends as care rather than oppression. Verses show Yusuf, after a life of reversals, declaring Allah his protector, and define the awliya as ordinary believers who have faith and taqwa, not otherworldly saints. He prefers 'ally' to 'friend', reads the qunut supplication as asking Allah to take us among those He protects, and explains the hadith qudsi in which Allah declares war on whoever harms His ally, reached through obligations first and then voluntary worship. Examples follow: Ibrahim in the fire, Pharaoh recognizing Musa's guardian too late, the cave of the Hijrah, and the companion whose body was shielded by wasps and a flood. The practical step is to become a protecting guardian for someone who is in need or voiceless, since Allah never lets His servant outdo Him in generosity.

outline.heading: Opening
Al-Wali versus Al-Wakil
outline.gist: Taking Allah as Wakil is an open contract sealed by your trust; Al-Wali is two-way, you choose Him and He must choose you back.

outline.heading: The guardian a child must bring
outline.gist: The Arabic school custom of bringing your wali shows the word; a child with no guardian at all is a picture of abandonment.

outline.heading: The wali in marriage is care
outline.gist: A bride's guardian signals that she is loved and protected; it is guardianship, not oppression.

outline.heading: Choosing Allah as protector: Yusuf's life
outline.gist: No one but the Creator who feeds and is not fed can be taken as guardian; Yusuf, after a life of reversals, declares Allah his protector.

outline.heading: Allah had already chosen Yusuf
outline.gist: The surah shows Allah protecting Yusuf throughout; the Prophet is told to say his guardian is Allah who protects the righteous.

outline.heading: Who are the awliya
outline.gist: No fear or grief for them: simply those who believe and have taqwa, not otherworldly figures radiating light.

outline.heading: The qunut supplication and the word ally
outline.gist: The Prophet's dua asks Allah to take us among those He takes as allies; 'friend of God' undersells the meaning.

outline.heading: Under His protection
outline.gist: Whoever harms Allah's ally deals with Him, so the believer can walk away from those who bother him; the relationship stays two-way.

outline.heading: Allah declares war on whoever harms His ally
outline.gist: A hadith qudsi in which Allah declares war on anyone hostile to His wali, one of very few such declarations.

outline.heading: How to become His ally
outline.gist: Obligations first, then continuous voluntary worship until Allah loves the servant, guides his senses, answers him and grants him refuge.

outline.heading: Ibrahim in the fire and Pharaoh drowning
outline.gist: Allah intervened for Ibrahim; Pharaoh only recognized who Musa's guardian was while drowning, when it was too late.

outline.heading: The cave of the Hijrah
outline.gist: The pursuers stood at the cave mouth and never looked down; if you do not support him, Allah already did.

outline.heading: The companion guarded by wasps and a flood
outline.gist: A companion killed by traitors asked Allah to protect his body from mutilation; wasps surrounded it and a flash flood carried it away forever.

outline.heading: Two hadith on those given responsibility
outline.gist: Anyone in a position of guardianship over Muslims who does not strive for them will not enter Paradise with them; the Prophet prayed against those who are harsh on those in their care.

outline.heading: Be someone's protecting guardian
outline.gist: Find someone in financial, spiritual or social need, or without a voice, and guard them; Allah will not be outdone in generosity.

outline.heading: From darkness into light
outline.gist: Allah is the guardian of believers and brings them from darkness to light, while other guardians lead from light to darkness.

TMKf-lIOY50.title: The Glorious Names of Allah: The All-Guiding, Al-Hadi
TMKf-lIOY50.one_line: Al-Hadi: the kinds of guidance Allah gives, how people come to faith, and living the name by seeking more guidance and guiding others.
TMKf-lIOY50.summary: He calls Al-Hadi the name Muslims are most attached to, since they ask for guidance at least seventeen times a day in Al-Fatihah. Hidayah means being led tenderly along a path. He lays out four kinds of guidance: the general guidance built into every creature, from migrating birds, bees and ants to the immune system; guidance to faith through innate moral knowledge, the primordial covenant, self-insight and the Quran; increase in guidance for those already guided; and guidance into Paradise. He shows that people reach faith in different ways: Umar over years, Abdullah ibn Salam at a single look at the Prophet's face, and Dimad on hearing the Prophet's opening words. Guidance, unlike provision, has no ceiling, so the prayer for it is repeated endlessly. He explains the parable of the straight path flanked by curtained doors with a caller at its end and a conscience above, and the Prophet's drawing of a person's lifespan, hopes and the hardships that strike him. He asks two things: be honest about the guidance you request daily and go seek it, since a prayer without action means little and knowledge that does not increase guidance only distances you; and ask Allah to use you as a door of guidance for others, without ever being replaced.

outline.heading: The name we ask by seventeen times a day
outline.gist: Every Muslim is attached to Al-Hadi daily; hidayah is tender guidance along a path.

outline.heading: Guidance always implies a path
outline.gist: The Arabs used hadi for a guide who leads you to your destination; Allah inspires every creature toward what benefits it and shows what is good.

outline.heading: Where the name appears in the Quran
outline.gist: Hadi appears a handful of times, as in none can guide whom Allah leaves astray and every people has a guide.

outline.heading: First type: general guidance in all creation
outline.gist: Musa's answer to Pharaoh, that his Lord gave everything its form and then guided it, ended the argument.

outline.heading: Birds, bees, ants and the immune system
outline.gist: Migrating birds, foraging bees, organised ants and immune cells that remember invaders all show creatures programmed to find their path; only humans take years.

outline.heading: Second type: guidance to faith through innate knowledge
outline.gist: Allah inspired the soul to know good and bad, and took the covenant from all of Adam's children, so we know lying and harm are wrong.

outline.heading: Self-insight and the Quran as guidance
outline.gist: We know ourselves fully but prefer comfortable lies about our sincerity and kindness; the Quran guides to what is most upright.

outline.heading: Third type: increase in guidance
outline.gist: Those who accept guidance are given more, as with the youths of the cave.

outline.heading: Fourth type: guidance to Paradise
outline.gist: In Jannah the people say praise be to Allah who guided us here; we would never have found it otherwise.

outline.heading: He guided you here before fajr
outline.gist: Who brought people to the masjid at 4:50 in the morning on Ramadan nights besides Allah, and it could be lost, since none can guide those who choose blindness.

outline.heading: Umar: guidance as a long process
outline.gist: From beating a Muslim girl who outlasted him, to listening secretly to the Quran at the Ka'bah, to his sister's house, it took years.

outline.heading: Abdullah ibn Salam: guidance in one glance
outline.gist: He prepared all night to expose the Prophet but on seeing his face said this is not the face of a liar.

outline.heading: Dimad: guidance through a few words
outline.gist: A man who claimed to cure possession came to treat the Prophet, heard his opening words of praise, asked him to repeat them and accepted Islam.

outline.heading: Guidance has no limit
outline.gist: Al-Fatihah is required in every rakah because we ask for guidance, which unlike provision, mercy or forgiveness can never be enough; the path can always get straighter.

outline.heading: Parable of the straight path and curtained doors
outline.gist: Walls with open doors behind curtains line the path; the path is Islam, curtains are Allah's limits, the caller is the Quran and the voice above is the conscience.

outline.heading: The Prophet's drawing of a lifespan and hopes
outline.gist: A square is the lifespan, a line beyond it the hopes, and small lines striking it are hardships that never stop coming.

outline.heading: First way to live it: seek what you ask for
outline.gist: Be honest about the guidance you request daily and go out seeking more each day, since dua without action means little; the path runs to the gates of Jannah.

outline.heading: The bridge mirrors how you walk now
outline.gist: How you walk the path in this life is how you will cross the sirat, quickly and steadily or stumbling.

outline.heading: Knowledge must increase guidance
outline.gist: Teach us what benefits us and benefit us with what we learn; knowledge that does not increase guidance only takes you farther from Allah.

outline.heading: Second way: be a door of guidance
outline.gist: Work for Allah by guiding people, knowing you cannot guide whom you love; guiding one person is better than owning the world.

outline.heading: Ask Allah not to replace you
outline.gist: His teacher thanked Allah after every lesson and asked Him to keep using him and not substitute someone else.

outline.heading: Those who bring people back are most beloved
outline.gist: The servants Allah loves most return the lost to Him; ask in Ramadan to be used for others' guidance so you keep your own.

61:7.ar: وَمَنۡ أَظۡلَمُ مِمَّنِ ٱفۡتَرَىٰ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ ٱلۡكَذِبَ وَهُوَ يُدۡعَىٰٓ إِلَى ٱلۡإِسۡلَٰمِۚ وَٱللَّهُ لَا يَهۡدِي ٱلۡقَوۡمَ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
61:7.en: And who doeth greater wrong than he who inventeth a lie against Allah when he is summoned unto Al-Islam? And Allah guideth not wrongdoing folk

61:8.ar: يُرِيدُونَ لِيُطۡفِـُٔواْ نُورَ ٱللَّهِ بِأَفۡوَٰهِهِمۡ وَٱللَّهُ مُتِمُّ نُورِهِۦ وَلَوۡ كَرِهَ ٱلۡكَٰفِرُونَ
61:8.en: Fain would they put out the light of Allah with their mouths, but Allah will perfect His light however much the disbelievers are averse

61:9.ar: هُوَ ٱلَّذِيٓ أَرۡسَلَ رَسُولَهُۥ بِٱلۡهُدَىٰ وَدِينِ ٱلۡحَقِّ لِيُظۡهِرَهُۥ عَلَى ٱلدِّينِ كُلِّهِۦ وَلَوۡ كَرِهَ ٱلۡمُشۡرِكُونَ
61:9.en: He it is Who hath sent His messenger with the guidance and the religion of truth, that He may make it conqueror of all religion however much idolaters may be averse

61:10.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ هَلۡ أَدُلُّكُمۡ عَلَىٰ تِجَٰرَةࣲ تُنجِيكُم مِّنۡ عَذَابٍ أَلِيمࣲ‏
61:10.en: O ye who believe! Shall I show you a commerce that will save you from a painful doom

61:11.ar: تُؤۡمِنُونَ بِٱللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِۦ وَتُجَٰهِدُونَ فِي سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ بِأَمۡوَٰلِكُمۡ وَأَنفُسِكُمۡۚ ذَٰلِكُمۡ خَيۡرࣱ لَّكُمۡ إِن كُنتُمۡ تَعۡلَمُونَ
61:11.en: Ye should believe in Allah and His messenger, and should strive for the cause of Allah with your wealth and your lives. That is better for you, if ye did but know

2:285.en: The messenger believeth in that which hath been revealed unto him from his Lord and (so do) believers. Each one believeth in Allah and His angels and His scriptures and His messengers - We make no distinction between any of His messengers - and they say: We hear, and we obey. 2:93.ar: وَإِذۡ أَخَذۡنَا مِيثَٰقَكُمۡ وَرَفَعۡنَا فَوۡقَكُمُ ٱلطُّورَ خُذُواْ مَآ ءَاتَيۡنَٰكُم بِقُوَّةࣲ وَٱسۡمَعُواْۖ قَالُواْ سَمِعۡنَا وَعَصَيۡنَا وَأُشۡرِبُواْ فِي قُلُوبِهِمُ ٱلۡعِجۡلَ بِكُفۡرِهِمۡۚ قُلۡ بِئۡسَمَا يَأۡمُرُكُم بِهِۦٓ إِيمَٰنُكُمۡ إِن كُنتُم مُّؤۡمِنِينَ
2:93.en: And when We made with you a covenant and caused the Mount to tower above you, (saying): Hold fast by that which We have given you, and hear (Our Word), they said: We hear and we rebel. And (worship of) the calf was made to sink into their hearts because of their rejection (of the covenant). Say (unto them): Evil is that which your belief enjoineth on you, if ye are believers

37:102.ar: فَلَمَّا بَلَغَ مَعَهُ ٱلسَّعۡيَ قَالَ يَٰبُنَيَّ إِنِّيٓ أَرَىٰ فِي ٱلۡمَنَامِ أَنِّيٓ أَذۡبَحُكَ فَٱنظُرۡ مَاذَا تَرَىٰۚ قَالَ يَٰٓأَبَتِ ٱفۡعَلۡ مَا تُؤۡمَرُۖ سَتَجِدُنِيٓ إِن شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ مِنَ ٱلصَّٰبِرِينَ
37:102.en: And when (his son) was old enough to walk with him, (Abraham) said: O my dear son, I have seen in a dream that I must sacrifice thee. So look, what thinkest thou? He said: O my father! Do that which thou art commanded. Allah willing, thou shalt find me of the steadfast

Q4Ig6y3LhWk.title: Tafseer of Surat As-Saff, Part 3: Verses 7-11
Q4Ig6y3LhWk.one_line: As-Saff 7-11 as articles of the Muslim social contract: never distorting revelation, Islam as the religion of truth, and the transaction of faith and striving.
Q4Ig6y3LhWk.summary: He frames Surat As-Saff as the Quran's statement of the social contract between a Muslim and the ummah, reviewing the articles from the first six verses: commit to what you say, stand equally in the rank, cause no harm, and carry the legacy forward. Verse 7 adds a fifth article. Dhulm means putting something where it does not belong, and the gravest form is lying in Allah's name by reshaping the faith to suit oneself. People will fall short in practice, and that is human, but the teaching itself must not be bent. Verse 8 describes such distortion as trying to blow out Allah's light, and verse 9 names Islam the religion of truth, which leads him to critique the post-2001 'religion of peace' messaging: Islam pursues what is right, which sometimes means peace and sometimes standing one's ground. Verses 10-11 present the contract itself as a transaction addressed directly to everyone, the Prophet included, so no leader is exempt from accountability. He notes the warning of punishment is stated first out of fairness, then explains the two terms: full acceptance of Allah and His Messenger, and striving with all one has and all one is. He ends by stressing that this deal is entirely in the believer's favour.

outline.heading: The cluster of surahs and the idea of a social contract
outline.gist: The surahs from Al-Mujadalah to As-Saff organise a Muslim's relationships; As-Saff sets out what a Muslim owes the ummah and what it owes him.

outline.heading: Review: the first articles from verses 1-6
outline.gist: Commitment to what you say, standing equally in the rank, causing no harm, and continuing the prophetic legacy.

outline.heading: Interlude
'Who does greater wrong': the rhetorical form
outline.gist: The question means no one is worse than the person described; it is a way of marking a grave wrong.

outline.heading: Dhulm as putting things out of their place
outline.gist: Oppression can be against oneself or creation; creation runs on a balance, and disturbing it causes harm one may not see yet, as ecosystems and the salmon run show.

outline.heading: Accepting a prohibition before understanding it
outline.gist: Like children arguing with parents, adults should stop doing what Allah forbids before grasping why, because some mistakes cannot be undone.

outline.heading: Lying in Allah's name while being called to Islam
outline.gist: Fabricating against Allah means attributing to Him what He did not say, by someone who belongs to the faith.

outline.heading: Fifth article: represent revelation as Allah intended
outline.gist: After the Prophet, the Quran must be read in line with itself, his life and the Arabic language; everything is done in Allah's name, so it must match His teaching.

outline.heading: No bargaining with revelation
outline.gist: The command not to say 'ra'ina' and the contrast between 'we hear and obey' and 'we hear and disobey': ask for time and help, never for the text to change.

outline.heading: Fall short in practice, but never change the faith
outline.gist: Everyone struggles with parts of Islam; the worst wrong is distorting it, which is why Muslims suffer most from extremism in either direction.

outline.heading: Trying to blow out Allah's light with their mouths
outline.gist: Distorting the message is an attempt to extinguish His light, but Allah completes it whether in the Prophet's lifetime or by Islam reaching every home.

outline.heading: The teacher's role and accepting uncomfortable verses
outline.gist: His job is only to convey what Allah meant; some verses will be hard, and one obeys anyway, as Ibrahim did when commanded to sacrifice his son.

outline.heading: Religion of truth, not 'religion of peace'
outline.gist: Allah calls Islam din al-haqq; it pursues peace or stands its ground depending on where right lies, and softening that after 2001 cost Muslims clarity.

outline.heading: Prevailing over all ways of life, despite those who hate it
outline.gist: Truth will rise above other laws regardless of anyone's dislike; following its rules is how a person discovers their potential.

outline.heading: Interlude
The contract as a tijarah: a transaction
outline.gist: Tijarah means an exchange where each side must deliver its full part to receive the other's.

outline.heading: Addressed directly, the Prophet included
outline.gist: Allah does not tell the Prophet to say this; the call includes him because he is party to the same contract.

outline.heading: Leaders are not exempt from the contract
outline.gist: Positions are added responsibility, not privilege; power without accountability corrupts everyone, so holding leaders to account protects them too, while today's politics has normalised lying.

outline.heading: Warning of punishment stated first
outline.gist: Fairness requires telling people the negative consequences up front; rewards can be a pleasant surprise, punishment cannot.

outline.heading: First term: iman as full acceptance
outline.gist: Accepting Allah and His Messenger and all they brought, with no cherry-picking; without it actions have no basis.

outline.heading: Second term: jihad as striving
outline.gist: Striving is moving forward against resistance: first against the self, then against evil, in doing good, and only rarely on the battlefield.

outline.heading: Striving with wealth and self
outline.gist: Wealth means everything you possess, from intellect to status; self means who you are, all spent for Allah.

outline.heading: 'That is best for you, if you only knew'
outline.gist: Living for something beyond yourself is best for you; this deal is never a rip-off for the believer, who gains in both lives far beyond what he gives.

themes.label: Justice and refusing oppression

themes.label: Obedience to Allah and the Messenger

themes.label: Methodology: how to read texts, tafsir method, intellectual approach
themes.note: Revelation must be represented as Allah intended, read in line with the Quran, the Sunnah and Arabic; distorting it is the gravest wrong.

themes.label: Extremism, bad religiosity and distorted practice
themes.note: Muslims suffer most from distortion, whether literalist extremism or abandoning the faith's content.

themes.label: Media and controlling the narrative
themes.note: The 'religion of peace' messaging after 2001 replaced Islam's own description as the religion of truth and weakened the conversation.

themes.label: Leadership, governance and institutions
themes.note: The Prophet is included in the contract; leaders carry extra responsibility and must be scrutinised, and modern politics has normalised corruption.

themes.note: Jihad is striving against resistance, starting with the self, using all one has and all one is.

themes.note: Iman here is full acceptance of Allah and His Messenger with no cherry-picking.

8:9.ar: إِذۡ تَسۡتَغِيثُونَ رَبَّكُمۡ فَٱسۡتَجَابَ لَكُمۡ أَنِّي مُمِدُّكُم بِأَلۡفࣲ مِّنَ ٱلۡمَلَٰٓئِكَةِ مُرۡدِفِينَ
8:9.en: When ye sought help of your Lord and He answered you (saying): I will help you with a thousand of the angels, rank on rank

8:10.ar: وَمَا جَعَلَهُ ٱللَّهُ إِلَّا بُشۡرَىٰ وَلِتَطۡمَئِنَّ بِهِۦ قُلُوبُكُمۡۚ وَمَا ٱلنَّصۡرُ إِلَّا مِنۡ عِندِ ٱللَّهِۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَزِيزٌ حَكِيمٌ
8:10.en: Allah appointed it only as good tidings, and that your hearts thereby might be at rest. Victory cometh only by the help of Allah. Lo! Allah is Mighty, Wise

3:126.ar: وَمَا جَعَلَهُ ٱللَّهُ إِلَّا بُشۡرَىٰ لَكُمۡ وَلِتَطۡمَئِنَّ قُلُوبُكُم بِهِۦۗ وَمَا ٱلنَّصۡرُ إِلَّا مِنۡ عِندِ ٱللَّهِ ٱلۡعَزِيزِ ٱلۡحَكِيمِ
3:126.en: Allah ordained this only as a message of good cheer for you, and that thereby your hearts might be at rest - Victory cometh only from Allah, the Mighty, the Wise

8:17.ar: فَلَمۡ تَقۡتُلُوهُمۡ وَلَٰكِنَّ ٱللَّهَ قَتَلَهُمۡۚ وَمَا رَمَيۡتَ إِذۡ رَمَيۡتَ وَلَٰكِنَّ ٱللَّهَ رَمَىٰ وَلِيُبۡلِيَ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ مِنۡهُ بَلَآءً حَسَنًاۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ سَمِيعٌ عَلِيمࣱ‏
8:17.en: Ye (Muslims) slew them not, but Allah slew them. And thou (Muhammad) threwest not when thou didst throw, but Allah threw, that He might test the believers by a fair test from Him. Lo! Allah is Hearer, Knower

8:42.ar: إِذۡ أَنتُم بِٱلۡعُدۡوَةِ ٱلدُّنۡيَا وَهُم بِٱلۡعُدۡوَةِ ٱلۡقُصۡوَىٰ وَٱلرَّكۡبُ أَسۡفَلَ مِنكُمۡۚ وَلَوۡ تَوَاعَدتُّمۡ لَٱخۡتَلَفۡتُمۡ فِي ٱلۡمِيعَٰدِ وَلَٰكِن لِّيَقۡضِيَ ٱللَّهُ أَمۡرࣰ ا كَانَ مَفۡعُولࣰ ا لِّيَهۡلِكَ مَنۡ هَلَكَ عَنۢ بَيِّنَةࣲ وَيَحۡيَىٰ مَنۡ حَيَّ عَنۢ بَيِّنَةࣲۗ وَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَسَمِيعٌ عَلِيمٌ
8:42.en: When ye were on the near bank (of the valley) and they were on the yonder bank, and the caravan was below you (on the coast plain). And had ye trysted to meet one another ye surely would have failed to keep the tryst, but (it happened, as it did, without the forethought of either of you) that Allah might conclude a thing that must be done; that he who perished (on that day) might perish by a clear proof (of His Sovereignty) and he who survived might survive by a clear proof (of His Sovereignty). Lo! Allah in truth is Hearer, Knower

8:43.ar: إِذۡ يُرِيكَهُمُ ٱللَّهُ فِي مَنَامِكَ قَلِيلࣰ اۖ وَلَوۡ أَرَىٰكَهُمۡ كَثِيرࣰ ا لَّفَشِلۡتُمۡ وَلَتَنَٰزَعۡتُمۡ فِي ٱلۡأَمۡرِ وَلَٰكِنَّ ٱللَّهَ سَلَّمَۚ إِنَّهُۥ عَلِيمُۢ بِذَاتِ ٱلصُّدُورِ
8:43.en: When Allah showed them unto thee (O Muhammad) in thy dream as few in number, and if He had shown them to thee as many, ye (Muslims) would have faltered and would have quarrelled over the affair. But Allah saved (you). Lo! He knoweth what is in the breasts (of men)

8:44.ar: وَإِذۡ يُرِيكُمُوهُمۡ إِذِ ٱلۡتَقَيۡتُمۡ فِيٓ أَعۡيُنِكُمۡ قَلِيلࣰ ا وَيُقَلِّلُكُمۡ فِيٓ أَعۡيُنِهِمۡ لِيَقۡضِيَ ٱللَّهُ أَمۡرࣰ ا كَانَ مَفۡعُولࣰ اۗ وَإِلَى ٱللَّهِ تُرۡجَعُ ٱلۡأُمُورُ
8:44.en: And when He made you (Muslims), when ye met (them), see them with your eyes as few, and lessened you in their eyes, (it was) that Allah might conclude a thing that must be done. Unto Allah all things are brought back

2:286.ar: لَا يُكَلِّفُ ٱللَّهُ نَفۡسًا إِلَّا وُسۡعَهَاۚ لَهَا مَا كَسَبَتۡ وَعَلَيۡهَا مَا ٱكۡتَسَبَتۡۗ رَبَّنَا لَا تُؤَاخِذۡنَآ إِن نَّسِينَآ أَوۡ أَخۡطَأۡنَاۚ رَبَّنَا وَلَا تَحۡمِلۡ عَلَيۡنَآ إِصۡرࣰ ا كَمَا حَمَلۡتَهُۥ عَلَى ٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبۡلِنَاۚ رَبَّنَا وَلَا تُحَمِّلۡنَا مَا لَا طَاقَةَ لَنَا بِهِۦۖ وَٱعۡفُ عَنَّا وَٱغۡفِرۡ لَنَا وَٱرۡحَمۡنَآۚ أَنتَ مَوۡلَىٰنَا فَٱنصُرۡنَا عَلَى ٱلۡقَوۡمِ ٱلۡكَٰفِرِينَ
2:286.en: Allah tasketh not a soul beyond its scope. For it (is only) that which it hath earned, and against it (only) that which it hath deserved. Our Lord! Condemn us not if we forget, or miss the mark! Our Lord! Lay not on us such a burden as thou didst lay on those before us! Our Lord! Impose not on us that which we have not the strength to bear! Pardon us, absolve us and have mercy on us, Thou, our Protector, and give us victory over the disbelieving folk

8:63.ar: وَأَلَّفَ بَيۡنَ قُلُوبِهِمۡۚ لَوۡ أَنفَقۡتَ مَا فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ جَمِيعࣰ ا مَّآ أَلَّفۡتَ بَيۡنَ قُلُوبِهِمۡ وَلَٰكِنَّ ٱللَّهَ أَلَّفَ بَيۡنَهُمۡۚ إِنَّهُۥ عَزِيزٌ حَكِيمࣱ‏
8:63.en: And (as for the believers) hath attuned their hearts. If thou hadst spent all that is in the earth thou couldst not have attuned their hearts, but Allah hath attuned them. Lo! He is Mighty, Wise

3:128.ar: لَيۡسَ لَكَ مِنَ ٱلۡأَمۡرِ شَيۡءٌ أَوۡ يَتُوبَ عَلَيۡهِمۡ أَوۡ يُعَذِّبَهُمۡ فَإِنَّهُمۡ ظَٰلِمُونَ
3:128.en: It is no concern at all of thee (Muhammad) whether He relent toward them or punish them; for they are evil-doers

8:11.ar: إِذۡ يُغَشِّيكُمُ ٱلنُّعَاسَ أَمَنَةࣰ مِّنۡهُ وَيُنَزِّلُ عَلَيۡكُم مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ مَآءࣰ لِّيُطَهِّرَكُم بِهِۦ وَيُذۡهِبَ عَنكُمۡ رِجۡزَ ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنِ وَلِيَرۡبِطَ عَلَىٰ قُلُوبِكُمۡ وَيُثَبِّتَ بِهِ ٱلۡأَقۡدَامَ
8:11.en: When He made the slumber fall upon you as a reassurance from him and sent down water from the sky upon you, that thereby He might purify you, and remove from you the fear of Satan, and make strong your hearts and firm (your) feet thereby

Z-VG4jwcAGs.speaker: adnan
Z-VG4jwcAGs.speaker_note: Single speaker continuing 'the series that I have started' on the laws of success from Surah Al-Anfal, recapping his own earlier khutbahs.
Z-VG4jwcAGs.title: The Laws of Success/Victory 6: Sparing No Effort
Z-VG4jwcAGs.one_line: From the Badr verses of Al-Anfal: Allah controls every outcome and detail, so our only job is to give full effort for His sake.
Z-VG4jwcAGs.summary: Continuing his Al-Anfal series, he recaps the laws covered so far (avoiding materialism, financial preparation and waqf, righteousness) and introduces the fourth: sparing no effort, which he says is the most repeated law and the least understood. He walks through the Badr verses. The angels were only good news, and 'you did not throw when you threw' means the Muslims released the arrow but Allah made it land. The battle was a space for them to prove their commitment. He then shows how many details Allah arranged that nobody could have planned: the caravan slipping away, the two banks, the rain turning one side to mud, the Prophet's dream showing the enemy as few, and each army seeing the other as smaller. Since outcomes are Allah's alone, it is incoherent to run at five percent and then ask why He has not fixed things; even at full capacity we have no claim on the result. The Prophet gave everything to uniting hearts and was still told it was Allah who united them. In the second khutbah he uses the sapling hadith: you are judged on effort, not outcome. Find your piece of the puzzle, dedicate yourself to it, and stop worrying about what you cannot control.

outline.heading: Opening
The laws so far
outline.gist: Of the twenty or so laws of success in Al-Anfal he will cover seven or eight; so far, avoiding materialism, preparation with a focus on finances and waqf, and righteousness.

outline.heading: The fourth law: sparing no effort
outline.gist: Trying your absolute best is the law the Quran repeats most, including in its accounts of Badr, yet it is poorly understood and practised; he will show where the missing link lies.

outline.heading: The angels were only good news
outline.gist: Allah answered the call at Badr with a thousand angels, then said this was only glad tidings, and repeats it for Uhud: victory comes from Allah alone, and such details are given to lift morale, not to be treated as the cause.

outline.heading: You did not throw when you threw
outline.gist: The verse sounds like a contradiction: they did fight and shoot, but you pulled the bow and let go, and it was Allah who made the arrow hit its target.

outline.heading: The battle is space to prove yourself
outline.gist: Then why act at all? To prove you truly believe and will try your ultimate best; the decree goes whichever way He wills and is not our business. Show me that you care enough.

outline.heading: Racing for the farther bank, and failing
outline.gist: The Muslims tried to reach the higher, firmer ground of the far bank and could not; they ended up on the nearer bank while the enemy took the high ground.

outline.heading: Abu Sufyan's caravan slips away unseen
outline.gist: The caravan diverted toward the Red Sea coast; neither side knew, and had the Muslims seen it they would have chased it and ruined everything.

outline.heading: Had you planned it, you would have failed
outline.gist: Had you arranged the meeting yourselves it would not have worked; Allah set it up so His decree would be carried out. There are infinite variables no human plan can account for.

outline.heading: The rain changed the ground
outline.gist: They planned as hard as they could and it still did not go their way, yet the rain turned the enemy's high ground to mud and firmed the sand beneath the Muslims.

outline.heading: The Prophet's dream: the enemy shown as few
outline.gist: Honest in reporting what he saw, the Prophet saw fewer than a thousand; had he seen and reported the real number, the 314 would have lost heart.

outline.heading: Each army saw the other as fewer
outline.gist: On the field the Muslims saw the enemy as less and lost their fear, while Quraysh saw the Muslims as fewer and grew careless and arrogant; Allah controls even how the brain reads what the eye sees.

outline.heading: It is not my business what He decrees
outline.gist: All matters return to Allah; I do not get to question, object or ask why when He accounts for details I cannot comprehend.

outline.heading: Full capacity, not five percent
outline.gist: Do your part at full capacity and you still have no claim on the outcome; running at five or ten percent and asking why He has not fixed everything is an intellectual contradiction.

outline.heading: Allah united their hearts
outline.gist: Spending all the wealth on earth could not have united them, yet uniting hearts was the Prophet's life work at full capacity; he was told it was Allah who did it.

outline.heading: Not your affair: the parallel verse on Uhud
outline.gist: Aal-Imran tells the Prophet that whether Allah punishes or forgives them is not his affair; our job is our full effort for the ummah, and even then we have no grounds to expect anything.

outline.heading: The nap and the rain before Badr
outline.gist: Details the Muslims could not arrange were Allah's preparation; He never needed our help running His universe. The question is whether we know our role and give full effort.

outline.heading: Interlude
Effort is who you are, not a side gig
outline.gist: Trying your best for Allah's satisfaction should be second nature to a Muslim, not something done in spare time.

outline.heading: The sapling hadith: judged on effort, not outcome
outline.gist: If the Hour comes and you hold a sapling, plant it; asking why shows you never understood. You are accountable for planning and effort, never for the outcome, so do not overcomplicate something dead simple.

outline.heading: Find your piece of the puzzle
outline.gist: Find the one thing that matters for you and dedicate yourself to it; like the man meeting Allah carrying the tree he died planting, know what you will bring.

outline.heading: Stop worrying about what you cannot control
outline.gist: You cannot control the Prophet's dream or the brain's perception; control yourself, how you live and what you commit to, and let Allah run His universe.

outline.heading: An unplanned mobilization: will you continue?
outline.gist: If everyone gave full effort the ummah's energy would converge even without organization, as when Muslims worldwide took to the streets in recent months; the agony has not ended, so will we continue?

outline.heading: Outro

themes.label: Tawakkul: reliance on Allah
themes.note: Victory and every detail of Badr were Allah's doing: the angels, the arrow finding its mark, the rain, the dream, the perception of numbers. Our part is effort; the decree is His and not ours to question.

themes.label: Work ethic, productivity and excellence (itqan)
themes.note: The law of the khutbah: run at 100 or 110 percent. Giving five percent and then complaining that Allah has not delivered is an intellectual contradiction of what the deen asks.

themes.label: Seerah events and their lessons
themes.note: A close reading of Badr through Al-Anfal: the race for the higher bank, Abu Sufyan's caravan diverting, the rain, the Prophet's dream of fewer enemies, and the nap before battle.

themes.label: Accountability before Allah and goals
themes.note: You are held accountable for your planning, effort and work, never for the outcome. The sapling hadith makes the point: do the right thing because that is who you are.

themes.label: Purpose, meaning and the point of life
themes.note: Find your piece of the puzzle, dedicate yourself to it, and be able to tell Allah what you lived and died trying to do for His sake. Answer that question and the rest follows.

themes.label: Unity of the ummah
themes.note: The Prophet's whole effort went into bringing hearts together, yet Allah says only He united them; human effort is required but the result belongs to Him.

themes.label: Community building, cooperation and the ummah
themes.note: If everyone gave full effort the ummah's energy would converge even without organization, as the unplanned worldwide mobilization of recent months showed. The question is whether people continue.

quran.point: Allah answered the Muslims' call at Badr with a thousand angels in succession.
The angels were only good news; victory comes from Allah alone, so do not treat the means as the cause.
The same statement repeated in Aal-Imran, which he returns to later to connect the Badr verses to Uhud.
You did not kill them, Allah did; you did not throw when you threw. We act, Allah makes it land; the battle is space to prove ourselves.
The nearer and farther banks and the caravan below; had you arranged the meeting you would have failed, but Allah set it up so His decree would be carried out.
Allah showed the enemy as few in the Prophet's dream; had He shown them as many, the Muslims would have lost heart.
Each army was made to look fewer in the other's eyes so Allah's decree would be fulfilled; all matters return to Allah.
He paraphrases 'the ayah' about your capacity: run at full capacity; that is all that is asked. Could equally be 64:16.
Had you spent all the wealth on earth you could not have united their hearts, but Allah united them, even though uniting hearts was the Prophet's life work.
Whether Allah punishes or forgives them is not your affair: the outcome is His, the effort is ours.
The drowsiness and the rain before Badr, details the Muslims could not have arranged.

19:96.en: Lo! those who believe and do good works, the Beneficent will appoint for them love

5:54.en: O ye who believe! Whoso of you becometh a renegade from his religion, (know that in his stead) Allah will bring a people whom He loveth and who love Him, humble toward believers, stern toward disbelievers, striving in the way of Allah, and fearing not the blame of any blamer. 52:48.ar: وَٱصۡبِرۡ لِحُكۡمِ رَبِّكَ فَإِنَّكَ بِأَعۡيُنِنَاۖ وَسَبِّحۡ بِحَمۡدِ رَبِّكَ حِينَ تَقُومُ
52:48.en: So wait patiently (O Muhammad) for thy Lord's decree, for surely thou art in Our sight; and hymn the praise of thy Lord when thou uprisest

3:35.ar: إِذۡ قَالَتِ ٱمۡرَأَتُ عِمۡرَٰنَ رَبِّ إِنِّي نَذَرۡتُ لَكَ مَا فِي بَطۡنِي مُحَرَّرࣰ ا فَتَقَبَّلۡ مِنِّيٓۖ إِنَّكَ أَنتَ ٱلسَّمِيعُ ٱلۡعَلِيمُ
3:35.en: (Remember) when the wife of 'Imran said: My Lord! I have vowed unto Thee that which is in my belly as a consecrated (offering). Accept it from me. Lo! Thou, only Thou, art the Hearer, the Knower

3:36.ar: فَلَمَّا وَضَعَتۡهَا قَالَتۡ رَبِّ إِنِّي وَضَعۡتُهَآ أُنثَىٰ وَٱللَّهُ أَعۡلَمُ بِمَا وَضَعَتۡ وَلَيۡسَ ٱلذَّكَرُ كَٱلۡأُنثَىٰۖ وَإِنِّي سَمَّيۡتُهَا مَرۡيَمَ وَإِنِّيٓ أُعِيذُهَا بِكَ وَذُرِّيَّتَهَا مِنَ ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنِ ٱلرَّجِيمِ
3:36.en: And when she was delivered she said: My Lord! Lo! I am delivered of a female - Allah knew best of what she was delivered - the male is not as the female; and lo! I have named her Mary, and lo! I crave Thy protection for her and for her offspring from Satan the outcast

3:37.ar: فَتَقَبَّلَهَا رَبُّهَا بِقَبُولٍ حَسَنࣲ وَأَنۢبَتَهَا نَبَاتًا حَسَنࣰ ا وَكَفَّلَهَا زَكَرِيَّاۖ كُلَّمَا دَخَلَ عَلَيۡهَا زَكَرِيَّا ٱلۡمِحۡرَابَ وَجَدَ عِندَهَا رِزۡقࣰ اۖ قَالَ يَٰمَرۡيَمُ أَنَّىٰ لَكِ هَٰذَاۖ قَالَتۡ هُوَ مِنۡ عِندِ ٱللَّهِۖ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَرۡزُقُ مَن يَشَآءُ بِغَيۡرِ حِسَابٍ
3:37.en: And her Lord accepted her with full acceptance and vouchsafed to her a goodly growth; and made Zachariah her guardian. Whenever Zachariah went into the sanctuary where she was, he found that she had food. He said: O Mary! Whence cometh unto thee this (food)? She answered: It is from Allah. Allah giveth without stint to whom He will

21:83.ar: ۞وَأَيُّوبَ إِذۡ نَادَىٰ رَبَّهُۥٓ أَنِّي مَسَّنِيَ ٱلضُّرُّ وَأَنتَ أَرۡحَمُ ٱلرَّٰحِمِينَ
21:83.en: And Job, when he cried unto his Lord, (saying): Lo! adversity afflicteth me, and Thou art Most Merciful of all who show mercy

21:87.ar: وَذَا ٱلنُّونِ إِذ ذَّهَبَ مُغَٰضِبࣰ ا فَظَنَّ أَن لَّن نَّقۡدِرَ عَلَيۡهِ فَنَادَىٰ فِي ٱلظُّلُمَٰتِ أَن لَّآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّآ أَنتَ سُبۡحَٰنَكَ إِنِّي كُنتُ مِنَ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
21:87.en: And (mention) Dhu'n-Nun, when he went off in anger and deemed that We had no power over him, but he cried out in the darkness, saying: There is no Allah save Thee. Be Thou Glorified! Lo! I have been a wrong-doer

5:101.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ لَا تَسۡـَٔلُواْ عَنۡ أَشۡيَآءَ إِن تُبۡدَ لَكُمۡ تَسُؤۡكُمۡ وَإِن تَسۡـَٔلُواْ عَنۡهَا حِينَ يُنَزَّلُ ٱلۡقُرۡءَانُ تُبۡدَ لَكُمۡ عَفَا ٱللَّهُ عَنۡهَاۗ وَٱللَّهُ غَفُورٌ حَلِيمࣱ‏
5:101.en: O ye who believe! Ask not of things which, if they were made unto you, would trouble you; but if ye ask of them when the Qur'an is being revealed, they will be made known unto you. Allah pardoneth this, for Allah is Forgiving, Clement

2:165.ar: وَمِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ مَن يَتَّخِذُ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ أَندَادࣰ ا يُحِبُّونَهُمۡ كَحُبِّ ٱللَّهِۖ وَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓاْ أَشَدُّ حُبࣰّ ا لِّلَّهِۗ وَلَوۡ يَرَى ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوٓاْ إِذۡ يَرَوۡنَ ٱلۡعَذَابَ أَنَّ ٱلۡقُوَّةَ لِلَّهِ جَمِيعࣰ ا وَأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ شَدِيدُ ٱلۡعَذَابِ
2:165.en: Yet of mankind are some who take unto themselves (objects of worship which they set as) rivals to Allah, loving them with a love like (that which is the due) of Allah (only) - those who believe are stauncher in their love for Allah - Oh, that those who do evil had but known, (on the day) when they behold the doom, that power belongeth wholly to Allah, and that Allah is severe in punishment

3:31.ar: قُلۡ إِن كُنتُمۡ تُحِبُّونَ ٱللَّهَ فَٱتَّبِعُونِي يُحۡبِبۡكُمُ ٱللَّهُ وَيَغۡفِرۡ لَكُمۡ ذُنُوبَكُمۡۚ وَٱللَّهُ غَفُورࣱ رَّحِيمࣱ‏
3:31.en: Say, (O Muhammad, to mankind): If ye love Allah, follow me; Allah will love you and forgive you your sins. Allah is Forgiving, Merciful

vqNwPeAytC4.speaker: adnan
vqNwPeAytC4.speaker_note: Glorious Names of Allah series, single voice, compares with the previous day's name
vqNwPeAytC4.title: The Glorious Names of Allah: The Most Loving, Al-Wadud
vqNwPeAytC4.one_line: Al-Wadud: Allah's love is shown in action, never turns to hatred, and calls us to love Him, speak to Him and love one another.
vqNwPeAytC4.summary: He presents Al-Wadud as one of the gentle names, appearing in the Quran once or twice depending on how scholars read the second instance. Wudd is the purest love, one that is never followed by resentment, and unlike hubb, which is a feeling, wudd is love expressed in action: a smile, a gift, kind treatment. Allah shows His servants love until they love Him with their whole hearts. Just as He presents Himself as Provider to the poor and Protector to the frightened, He presents Himself as Al-Wadud to those who need love, which children need more than food or education. His love is general, seen in the beauty of creation and the affection placed between spouses, and specific, given to those who believe and do good, though He needs nothing from them. He points to revelation beginning with Jibril's embrace, and to a form of speaking with Allah beyond asking, shown by the mother of Maryam, Ayyub, Yunus and the Prophet at Ta'if, who simply told Allah their state. Hadith follow on Allah running to those who walk to Him, the shade for those who love for His sake, and the minbars of light for such people. He closes with three things to do: fill your heart with His love, draw near through acts of love that benefit people, and love fully, as Ramadan is itself a gesture of His love.

outline.heading: Opening
A gentle name after a name of might
outline.gist: Some names speak of power, others of beauty and compassion; Al-Wadud appears twice, though some scholars count only one.

outline.heading: Wudd: love never followed by hatred
outline.gist: Wudd is the purest, clearest love, one that never turns into vengeance as human love often does.

outline.heading: Hubb is a feeling, wudd is an action
outline.gist: Wudd sits high among the levels of love; feeling happy to see you is hubb, smiling, giving a gift and treating you well is wudd.

outline.heading: He shows love until we love Him
outline.gist: The name is not sentimental; Allah keeps showing His servants love until they love Him with all their hearts.

outline.heading: The name He shows when you need love
outline.gist: He presents Himself as Provider when you are poor and Protector when you are afraid, and as Al-Wadud when you need love.

outline.heading: Children need love above all
outline.gist: A child can survive hunger, old clothes or no schooling, but without love cannot function as an adult; we all need to be loved.

outline.heading: General love: beauty in creation
outline.gist: He placed beauty in everything He made, beyond necessity, as love shown to all, believers or not.

outline.heading: Love between spouses and even enemies
outline.gist: He placed affection and mercy between spouses of any faith, and may place love between you and your enemies.

outline.heading: Specific love for believers who do good
outline.gist: The Most Merciful will appoint love for those who believe and do good; He seeks His servants in love while needing nothing from them.

outline.heading: He loves them and they love Him
outline.gist: Describing the people He brings in place of those who turn back, Allah begins with His love for them.

outline.heading: You are within Our eyes
outline.gist: Allah told the struggling Prophet to be patient for he was in His eyes, an Arabic expression of deep love.

outline.heading: The deen began with a hug
outline.gist: On nights like these in Ramadan revelation started with Jibril embracing the Prophet; firm, but still an embrace.

outline.heading: Speaking to Allah beyond asking: the mother of Maryam
outline.gist: Shakwa is telling Allah your state; she explained she had borne a girl and named her, though He knew, because of the closeness she had with Him.

outline.heading: Ayyub and Yunus state their condition
outline.gist: Ayyub said harm had touched him and Allah is most merciful; Yunus declared Allah's oneness and his own wrong, neither asking for anything.

outline.heading: The Prophet's complaint at Ta'if
outline.gist: Bleeding, he told Allah of his weakness, his few means and how people disrespected him.

outline.heading: Come walking and He comes running
outline.gist: Draw near a hand-span and He draws near an arm's length; come walking and He comes running, all figurative.

outline.heading: Allah's word to Dawud about those who turn away
outline.gist: If those turning away knew His longing for their return they would melt in love; imagine His love for those coming close.

outline.heading: Shade for those who love for His sake
outline.gist: On Judgment Day Allah calls those who loved one another for Him and shades them; whoever loves his brother more is loved more by Allah.

outline.heading: Neither prophets nor martyrs, yet envied by them
outline.gist: A bedouin begged to know who they are: people of different lands with no kinship or trade between them who love one another for Allah, on minbars of light.

outline.heading: You will be with those you love
outline.gist: The man who prepared only love of Allah and His Messenger for the Hour; believers love Allah most, and following the Prophet earns His love.

outline.heading: First: fill your heart with His love
outline.gist: Only Allah's love fills the heart's void and calms it; notice His love reaching you every day.

outline.heading: Second: draw near through acts of love
outline.gist: Answer His love with actions; the most beloved to Allah are those most beneficial to His creation.

outline.heading: Third: love with all your heart
outline.gist: The Quran and Sunnah seem to ask only that we love Him back fully, not half-heartedly; Ramadan itself is a gesture of His love.

8:10.ar: وَمَا جَعَلَهُ ٱللَّهُ إِلَّا بُشۡرَىٰ وَلِتَطۡمَئِنَّ بِهِۦ قُلُوبُكُمۡۚ وَمَا ٱلنَّصۡرُ إِلَّا مِنۡ عِندِ ٱللَّهِۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَزِيزٌ حَكِيمٌ
8:10.en: Allah appointed it only as good tidings, and that your hearts thereby might be at rest. Victory cometh only by the help of Allah. Lo! Allah is Mighty, Wise

8:11.ar: إِذۡ يُغَشِّيكُمُ ٱلنُّعَاسَ أَمَنَةࣰ مِّنۡهُ وَيُنَزِّلُ عَلَيۡكُم مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ مَآءࣰ لِّيُطَهِّرَكُم بِهِۦ وَيُذۡهِبَ عَنكُمۡ رِجۡزَ ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنِ وَلِيَرۡبِطَ عَلَىٰ قُلُوبِكُمۡ وَيُثَبِّتَ بِهِ ٱلۡأَقۡدَامَ
8:11.en: When He made the slumber fall upon you as a reassurance from him and sent down water from the sky upon you, that thereby He might purify you, and remove from you the fear of Satan, and make strong your hearts and firm (your) feet thereby

33:25.ar: وَرَدَّ ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ بِغَيۡظِهِمۡ لَمۡ يَنَالُواْ خَيۡرࣰ اۚ وَكَفَى ٱللَّهُ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ ٱلۡقِتَالَۚ وَكَانَ ٱللَّهُ قَوِيًّا عَزِيزࣰ ا
33:25.en: And Allah repulsed the disbelievers in their wrath; they gained no good. Allah averted their attack from the believers. Allah is ever Strong, Mighty

9:40.ar: إِلَّا تَنصُرُوهُ فَقَدۡ نَصَرَهُ ٱللَّهُ إِذۡ أَخۡرَجَهُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ ثَانِيَ ٱثۡنَيۡنِ إِذۡ هُمَا فِي ٱلۡغَارِ إِذۡ يَقُولُ لِصَٰحِبِهِۦ لَا تَحۡزَنۡ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ مَعَنَاۖ فَأَنزَلَ ٱللَّهُ سَكِينَتَهُۥ عَلَيۡهِ وَأَيَّدَهُۥ بِجُنُودࣲ لَّمۡ تَرَوۡهَا وَجَعَلَ كَلِمَةَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ ٱلسُّفۡلَىٰۗ وَكَلِمَةُ ٱللَّهِ هِيَ ٱلۡعُلۡيَاۗ وَٱللَّهُ عَزِيزٌ حَكِيمٌ
9:40.en: If ye help him not, still Allah helped him when those who disbelieve drove him forth, the second of two; when they two were in the cave, when he said unto his comrade: Grieve not. Lo! Allah is with us. Then Allah caused His peace of reassurance to descend upon him and supported him with hosts ye cannot see, and made the word of those who disbelieved the nethermost, while Allah's Word it was that became the uppermost. Allah is Mighty, Wise

67:2.ar: ٱلَّذِي خَلَقَ ٱلۡمَوۡتَ وَٱلۡحَيَوٰةَ لِيَبۡلُوَكُمۡ أَيُّكُمۡ أَحۡسَنُ عَمَلࣰ اۚ وَهُوَ ٱلۡعَزِيزُ ٱلۡغَفُورُ
67:2.en: Who hath created life and death that He may try you which of you is best in conduct; and He is the Mighty, the Forgiving

57:1.ar: سَبَّحَ لِلَّهِ مَا فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِۖ وَهُوَ ٱلۡعَزِيزُ ٱلۡحَكِيمُ
57:1.en: All that is in the heavens and the earth glorifieth Allah; and He is the Mighty, the Wise

5:116.ar: وَإِذۡ قَالَ ٱللَّهُ يَٰعِيسَى ٱبۡنَ مَرۡيَمَ ءَأَنتَ قُلۡتَ لِلنَّاسِ ٱتَّخِذُونِي وَأُمِّيَ إِلَٰهَيۡنِ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِۖ قَالَ سُبۡحَٰنَكَ مَا يَكُونُ لِيٓ أَنۡ أَقُولَ مَا لَيۡسَ لِي بِحَقٍّۚ إِن كُنتُ قُلۡتُهُۥ فَقَدۡ عَلِمۡتَهُۥۚ تَعۡلَمُ مَا فِي نَفۡسِي وَلَآ أَعۡلَمُ مَا فِي نَفۡسِكَۚ إِنَّكَ أَنتَ عَلَّٰمُ ٱلۡغُيُوبِ
5:116.en: And when Allah saith: O Jesus, son of Mary! Didst thou say unto mankind: Take me and my mother for two gods beside Allah? he saith: Be glorified! It was not mine to utter that to which I had no right. If I used to say it, then Thou knewest it. Thou knowest what is in my mind, and I know not what is in Thy Mind. Lo! Thou, only Thou, art the Knower of Things Hidden

5:117.ar: مَا قُلۡتُ لَهُمۡ إِلَّا مَآ أَمَرۡتَنِي بِهِۦٓ أَنِ ٱعۡبُدُواْ ٱللَّهَ رَبِّي وَرَبَّكُمۡۚ وَكُنتُ عَلَيۡهِمۡ شَهِيدࣰ ا مَّا دُمۡتُ فِيهِمۡۖ فَلَمَّا تَوَفَّيۡتَنِي كُنتَ أَنتَ ٱلرَّقِيبَ عَلَيۡهِمۡۚ وَأَنتَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيۡءࣲ شَهِيدٌ
5:117.en: I spake unto them only that which Thou commandedst me, (saying): Worship Allah, my Lord and your Lord. I was a witness of them while I dwelt among them, and when Thou tookest me Thou wast the Watcher over them. Thou art Witness over all things

5:118.ar: إِن تُعَذِّبۡهُمۡ فَإِنَّهُمۡ عِبَادُكَۖ وَإِن تَغۡفِرۡ لَهُمۡ فَإِنَّكَ أَنتَ ٱلۡعَزِيزُ ٱلۡحَكِيمُ
5:118.en: If Thou punish them, lo! they are Thy slaves, and if Thou forgive them (lo! they are Thy slaves). Lo! Thou, only Thou, art the Mighty, the Wise

2:260.ar: وَإِذۡ قَالَ إِبۡرَٰهِـۧمُ رَبِّ أَرِنِي كَيۡفَ تُحۡيِ ٱلۡمَوۡتَىٰۖ قَالَ أَوَلَمۡ تُؤۡمِنۖ قَالَ بَلَىٰ وَلَٰكِن لِّيَطۡمَئِنَّ قَلۡبِيۖ قَالَ فَخُذۡ أَرۡبَعَةࣰ مِّنَ ٱلطَّيۡرِ فَصُرۡهُنَّ إِلَيۡكَ ثُمَّ ٱجۡعَلۡ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ جَبَلࣲ مِّنۡهُنَّ جُزۡءࣰ ا ثُمَّ ٱدۡعُهُنَّ يَأۡتِينَكَ سَعۡيࣰ اۚ وَٱعۡلَمۡ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَزِيزٌ حَكِيمࣱ‏
2:260.en: And when Abraham said (unto his Lord): My Lord! Show me how Thou givest life to the dead, He said: Dost thou not believe? Abraham said: Yea, but (I ask) in order that my heart may be at ease. (His Lord) said: Take four of the birds and cause them to incline unto thee, then place a part of them on each hill, then call them, they will come to thee in haste, and know that Allah is Mighty, Wise

jlSNXrs7QLE.title: The Glorious Names of Allah: The Almighty, Al-Aziz
jlSNXrs7QLE.one_line: Al-Aziz: Allah is invincible, unparalleled, unquestioned and unfathomable, all honour is His, so live with dignity before people and humility before Him.
jlSNXrs7QLE.summary: He promises that understanding Al-Aziz should leave people more confident and stronger. The name appears ninety-five times and comes from izzah, which spans honour, glory, strength and pride. He gives it four meanings that no single English word captures: invincible, unparalleled, unquestioned and unfathomable. It is paired with eleven other names, most often the All-Wise, then the Most Merciful, the Strong and the All-Knowing, and each pairing reassures: such power is never reckless, cruel, weak or ignorant. He traces the name after the victories of Badr, the Trench and the Hijrah, after the verse that life and death were created as a test, at the end of the verses of glorification, and in two passages he enjoys: Isa ending his plea about his followers with you are the Almighty, the Wise rather than the Forgiving, since no one may question Allah if He pardons, and Ibrahim being told to know that Allah is Almighty when he asked how the dead are raised. All honour belongs to Allah, so seeking it from enemies or wealth fails, as the humiliated Aziz of Egypt shows. He asks three things: walk with your head high and never abase yourself before the rich, abase yourself before Allah in dua as the Prophet did, and stand by others so no one is left humiliated.

outline.heading: Opening
A name that makes you stronger
outline.gist: Understood properly it leaves you more confident; it appears ninety-five times and comes from izzah.

outline.heading: The four meanings of Al-Aziz
outline.gist: Izzah spans honour, glory, strength and pride; Allah is invincible, unparalleled, unquestioned in what He does and unfathomable.

outline.heading: Paired with eleven names
outline.gist: More pairings than any other name; four dominate: the All-Wise forty-seven times, the Most Merciful fourteen, the Strong seven and the All-Knowing six.

outline.heading: Paired with the All-Wise: never reckless
outline.gist: Unbelievable power might seem reckless, so it is paired with wisdom.

outline.heading: Paired with the Most Merciful: never cruel
outline.gist: Lest one fear cruelty from such power, He is extremely merciful.

outline.heading: Paired with the Strong: never weak
outline.gist: In verses about defeating enemies, being unparalleled would mean nothing without strength.

outline.heading: Paired with the All-Knowing: never ignorant
outline.gist: He uses His strength in the best ways because He knows all.

outline.heading: After the victory at Badr
outline.gist: The rain, the brief sleep and the ground beneath their feet were only good news; victory comes only from Allah, the Almighty.

outline.heading: After the Battle of the Trench
outline.gist: The passage ends with Allah turning back the confederates in their rage and sparing the believers from fighting.

outline.heading: After the Hijrah
outline.gist: Against all odds the Prophet reached Madinah, and the verse on that victory closes with Allah being Almighty and Wise.

outline.heading: Why we were created
outline.gist: The question philosophers cannot answer is met in Al-Mulk: He created death and life to test you, and He is the Almighty, beyond our grasp.

outline.heading: Glorification we cannot see
outline.gist: Surahs opening with everything glorifying Allah end with Al-Aziz: how it happens is unfathomable and not ours to question.

outline.heading: Isa: you are the Almighty, the Wise
outline.gist: Accused of what he forbade, Isa says if You forgive them, You are the Almighty, the Wise, not the Forgiving, because none may question Allah if He pardons them.

outline.heading: Ibrahim and the birds
outline.gist: Asking how Allah revives the dead, Ibrahim is told to know that Allah is Almighty: the how is beyond human analysis.

outline.heading: All honour belongs to Allah
outline.gist: Whoever seeks honour should know it all belongs to Allah; why seek it from enemies as allies when it is with Him.

outline.heading: The humiliated Aziz of Egypt
outline.gist: The Quran's man titled Al-Aziz was humiliated in his own home; honour sought outside Allah is an illusion.

outline.heading: First: live with dignity
outline.gist: You are the servant of Al-Aziz, so walk and ask with your head high; abasing yourself before the rich costs two thirds of your religion, and fear of death or poverty has no place.

outline.heading: Second: abase yourself before Allah
outline.gist: Ask Him by His might and your lowliness, as the Prophet did, head bowed with tears on his beard.

outline.heading: Third: give others dignity
outline.gist: Whoever stands by while a Muslim is humiliated will be humiliated before all creation; remind people not to abase themselves before anyone but Allah.

8:5.en: Even as thy Lord caused thee (Muhammad) to go forth from thy home with the Truth, and lo! a party of the believers were averse (to it)

8:6.ar: يُجَٰدِلُونَكَ فِي ٱلۡحَقِّ بَعۡدَ مَا تَبَيَّنَ كَأَنَّمَا يُسَاقُونَ إِلَى ٱلۡمَوۡتِ وَهُمۡ يَنظُرُونَ
8:6.en: Disputing with thee of the Truth after it had been made manifest, as if they were being driven to death visible

8:7.ar: وَإِذۡ يَعِدُكُمُ ٱللَّهُ إِحۡدَى ٱلطَّآئِفَتَيۡنِ أَنَّهَا لَكُمۡ وَتَوَدُّونَ أَنَّ غَيۡرَ ذَاتِ ٱلشَّوۡكَةِ تَكُونُ لَكُمۡ وَيُرِيدُ ٱللَّهُ أَن يُحِقَّ ٱلۡحَقَّ بِكَلِمَٰتِهِۦ وَيَقۡطَعَ دَابِرَ ٱلۡكَٰفِرِينَ
